checks.diagnosis: The prompt allows cuts that split a determiner/numeral/pronoun from the noun phrase it heads, breaking NP cohesion.
checks.evidence: de_de_445, de_de_1339, de_de_278, de_de_332 — all show the policy cutting between an initial determiner/quantifier/pronoun and its noun phrase, while the measured target keeps that determiner+NP intact.
checks.type_predicate: Positions that separate a sentence-initial determiner, numeral, or pronoun from the immediately following noun phrase it determines (i.e., a split between a determiner/quantifier/pronoun and its head NP).

edit.text: Avoid cutting between a determiner/numeral/pronoun and the noun phrase it determines; keep the determiner and its NP together.

orders.diagnosis: When two candidate cuts fall inside the same NP, the prompt misorders them — it sometimes prefers the later NP-tail cut but should prefer an earlier punctuation-separated cut when that preserves a complete clause.
orders.evidence: de_de_357, de_de_191, de_de_729 — each has two intra-NP candidate markers where the correct segmentation prefers the marker that preserves a self-contained clause at punctuation (or else preserves the NP as a unit), but the prompt chose the other order.
orders.type_predicate: Sentences containing two candidate markers inside the same noun phrase where one marker is immediately before punctuation (comma or sentence boundary) that would leave the left side a complete clause and the other lies elsewhere inside that NP.

edit.text: When two markers lie inside the same NP, if one is immediately before punctuation that yields a self-contained left clause prefer that earlier cut; otherwise prefer the later cut that keeps the NP head with its postmodifiers.
